newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Golden Hope eyeing Vietnam expansions.
newsitem.headline: Golden Hope eyeing Vietnam expansions.

text.p: Malaysia's Golden Hope Plantations Bhd said on Wednesday it planned to triple the size of its existing palm oil refinery in Vietnam and build a brand-new plant in order to meet strong demand.

The company will submit its application to the Vietnamese authorities soon and approval is expected by year-end, Golden Hope group chief executive Abdul Rahman Ramli told reporters after the company's annual meeting.
"It will be similar in size to the first plant," he said, adding that capital investment in the refinery is estimated at $9 million.

The first refinery, a joint venture with Vietnamese partners in which Golden Hope owns a 51 percent stake, started operations in 1993. It recorded a turnover of $22.3 million for the year ended June 30, 1996.
"We now have 30 to 35 percent market share," Abdul Rahman said.

He said with increasing competition and more foreign ventures being set up in Vietnam, the company plans to increase the capacity at the refinery to 150,000 tonnes a year from the present 50,000 tonnes to ensure its market share will be maintained.
